text:
jordan: FYI invoice-preview is showing a consistent ~6% undercount for streaming-heavy tenants after clientlib v3 rolled last night. flagging because billing saw a few customer questions.
lee: interesting, undercount vs yesterday? any specific routes or all streaming sessions?
jordan: mostly streaming routes (chat-stream, ws-gen). non-streams look stable. preview diff: 
```
+tenant: org-omega
-preview_tokens: 2,310,900
-current_preview: 2,176,400
-delta: -134,500 (-5.8%)
```
maria: clientlib v3 changed the sampling window from 60s -> 10s to reduce memory on mobile. that could lower token attribution for long sessions that previously had periodic heartbeats.
billing: timeline? we need to communicate if this will touch invoices or just preview.
jordan: invoices already generated for some mid-day batches; previews are for later-day billing. Historically we've seen previews correct prior to invoice cutoff but this looks systemic for streaming tenants.
ingest-bot: anomaly detector: detected drop in sampled_token_rate for route=chat-stream starting 1767560000, z-score=4.1. (ids: AD-176760).
lee: ok, two axes: (A) fix collection to preserve previous sampling semantics, (B) if not possible quickly, backfill to adjust tokens for affected windows. Which is cheaper operationally?
maria: revert to 60s is easy in config but increases mem usage on client. not ideal to force mobile clients to allocate more state. alternative: make sampling deterministic per session id so sample fraction stable across restarts.
jordan: we also need to ensure console explanation is clear. product asked for a per-tenant "sampling_change_impact" flag and an estimated delta line in preview if backfill is pending.
prod-analytics: quick ask: can you dump a 24h histogram of tokens-per-session before/after? i want to measure which sessions are affected (long tail).
jordan: attaching quick sample (pulled from logs): 
```
session_id: s-9f3a | tokens_prev_60s: 24,500 | tokens_10s_sampled: 1,200
session_id: s-7b2d | tokens_prev_60s: 4,200 | tokens_10s_sampled: 3,900
```
shows fragmentation: long-lived sessions get undersampled.
lee: proposed short-term: server-side patch to clientlib telemetry ingest: if event includes `clientlib_v="3"` and `session_duration>30s`, inflate sampled tokens by estimator factor (tokens_est = tokens_sampled * (60/10)). conservative cap at +20% to avoid over-correction.
maria: that feels hacky and may bias for some clients. better: deterministic reservoir sampling using session_id hash -> sample every Nth second to approximate 60s window while keeping footprint. implementation: sample if hash(session_id) % 6 == 0 given v3 defaults. deterministic and stable.
jordan: that would preserve token coverage for long sessions without memory increase. do we need client changes? server-only can map incoming short-window samples into a deterministic stream and accept samples if they match the hash. but if clients are already sampling at 10s we may still miss tokens unless they send enough samples.
prod-analytics: deterministic scheme sounds clean. we can simulate effect on historical logs quickly. give me 1-2 hours.
billing: assuming deterministic fix: do we need invoice adjustments? if previews before cut already undercounted, we'd have to run a correction backfill for the impacted invoice windows. finance prefers a single adjustment line per tenant with reason code `sampling_window_fix` rather than lots of micro-adjustments.
jordan: agree. backfill plan: (1) run deterministic-sim on raw client events to reconstruct expected sampled set (2) compute delta tokens by tenant and time window (3) emit correction invoice rows tagged `adjustment:sampling_window_fix` and post to invoice-preview feed and ledger as offsets.
lee: potential blocker: raw client events only kept for 7 days in hot storage. any tenants outside retention window won't be backfillable. we'll need to mark those as `estimated_adjustment` with an audit note.
maria: ops step: roll deterministic ingest rule to canary (5% of traffic) then 25% then 100% across regions. ingest-bot: scheduled canary at 2024-04-15T06:00Z -> 5% -> 06:30Z -> 25% -> 07:00Z -> 100%.
prod-analytics: simulation results: deterministic sampling recovers ~92% of missing tokens in our sample set. residuals cluster around very short bursts that are inherently missed.
billing: ok finance note: we'll provide estimated adjustment CSV and a narrative. customers with >2% invoice change will get an email draft for review.
jordan: UI ask: console needs a banner on tenant billing pages saying "We detected clientlib sampling change; invoice corrections pending" with link to audit log. Also add a toggle in preview to view pre-fix vs post-fix numbers.
lee: I can add the preview toggle card. product-approved?
prod-analytics: approved. also add a telemetry metric `sampling_recovery_rate` and an alert if recovery <80% in canary.
ingest-bot: note: created job J-176760-SIM to run deterministic sim nightly for 48h.
maria: timeline recap: (A) prod-analytics sim in 2h (B) ingest deterministic canary 06:00Z (C) if canary recovery >85% -> backfill compute job in 48h (D) invoice adjustments published and console banner visible before adjustments land.
jordan: thanks. I'm documenting comms for finance and support. will attach CSV once backfill runs. :slightly_smiling_face:
billing: appreciated. keep us looped for wording.
prod-analytics: will post the sim results in this thread when ready.
ingest-bot: anomaly AD-176760 marked in snapshot; linking J-176760-SIM and ticket BILL-6123.
